rows.what the ink shows: Immediately after the closing curve is a short rounded dark drop touching the slip edge. Its lower continuation is covered, so the exposed remnant does not securely distinguish a comma from another covered continuation.

The superposed capital has a dense vertical stem, upper and middle right bars, a lower right bar and a left lower loop. These surviving E-like and looped strokes cannot be assigned securely to a distinct earlier F beneath the overwriting.

The long lower cancellation after total retains isolated stems and hooks, but its connected word bodies and right-hand ending are merged with the heavy strike. The compact upper crossing with a descender, upright and acute-like dash is a separate written layer; those upper strokes cannot establish the marked lower engendré.

Below the slip edge only short connected low rises and a tall final stem with a rightward exit remain exposed. The beginning and upper portions of the word are physically covered, preventing a complete letter-by-letter reading of normale.

After the crossed telle que, a tall loop and separate raised specks survive above the heavy horizontal strike, followed by a pointed rise and dotted low strokes. The intervening bodies and word joins are buried, so the full l’on ait sequence and its boundary with the following residue remain uncertain.

The far-right deleted residue has a low pointed rise, several short basal turns and a descending terminal stroke underneath the continuous cancellation. No complete word bodies survive to recover the proposed two-word span or securely subdivide it from the preceding erased phrase.

The older index after the baseline a is densely blacked out; a dot and several slanted remnants remain but do not determine its glyph count or i/j identity. Below that blot, a separate circle encloses one short dotted i with a hooked foot; both the cancelled layer and this insertion are visible.

The cancelled coefficient has a small upper oval and a rightward stem, while diagonal and horizontal deletion strokes fill the lower area. Its baseline body and individual i/j subscript strokes cannot all be separated from those crossings, unlike the distinct rewritten coefficient to the right.

A left upright/hook, one high dot and a later short upright survive above the heavy horizontal cancellation. The intervening low bodies needed to distinguish s-o-i are merged into that cancellation, so the complete word soit is not securely recoverable.

The crossed word has a looped initial d, a separate raised apostrophe, a small o loop and a following low vowel body with a detached accent above it. These separated upper marks differ from the uninterrupted d-on-c outline of the uncrossed donc on the preceding line.

Immediately after Hadamard, the punctuation is a thick curved upright with two left-facing lobes and a short lower return, adjoining the closing-parenthesis position. No isolated lower dot or unambiguous straight exclamation stroke survives separately enough to choose ! over ?.

The word begins with a short hooked body, followed by low detached dashes and two taller late upturns with long rightward exits. The middle is compressed, and neither a distinct descending g for rectangle nor the complete co/n and final i-t sequence for construit can be separated securely.

The first slanting marginal word has a large angular A with a lower loop, then a low connecting stroke and a later tall crossed group. Substantial opening strokes are exposed; the faint/compressed suffix and its terminal portion at the slip edge do not establish all of jouter.

The next slanting group begins with a descending hooked p-like stroke, has several exposed but faint low connections and a later tall looped stroke. Its far end rises into the slip boundary; the accent and separate middle bodies needed for préambule are not secure, even in the exposed portion.

Between the second marginal group and the clear que/X line, a short angled fragment and curved descending trace remain beside the slip edge. The indistinct exposed traces and unavailable continuation prevent recovering a lexical reading or verifying the inherited placeholder count of one.

M1239 preserves the separately visible cancelled and circled inserted layers. The ellipsis is an editorial unknown-fragment placeholder and makes no glyph-count claim.
Initial own-ink report retained before independent peer adjudication.
